scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the right or wrong here. Let me start by laying out the situation as I see it. My dad came up with this business idea, and when I heard it, I was really impressed. It was simple yet genius. But I didn't think he could pull it off because he's more of an ideas person but not so good at executing them. I mean, he's intelligent, but he lacks the drive to get things done. I, on the other hand, am more action-oriented. I took his idea, got the IP rights, and started the business two years ago. It's been a massive success, making six figures and with the potential to make millions in the next few years. When I first did this, my dad was upset but didn't say much. My mom was proud and thought I did the right thing. I confronted him recently, and he called me a "fucking asshole," saying he felt betrayed and almost cried. I told him he's a man of ideas and I'm a man of action. My sister defended him, but my mom and granddad support me. I even offered him 20% of the profits, but he rejected it and told me to get out. I understand his feelings, but I think he's being unreasonable. I mean, I took his idea and made it successful. Shouldn't he be proud? Or is it wrong to take his idea without his consent? Hmm, maybe I should consider the ethical side. Did I steal his idea? Or was it more about taking an idea that he wasn't going to act on and making it a reality? I think the key here is whether I had permission or if I just took it without his knowledge. If he didn't give me permission, then technically, it's stealing. But if he just mentioned it as an idea and I ran with it, maybe it's a bit of both. Also, family dynamics play a big role here. My dad feels betrayed, which is a strong emotion. I can see why he would feel that way because I took something he came up with and used it for my own gain without his involvement. Even though I offered him a share, he might feel that it's not enough or that I disrespected him by not involving him from the start. On the other hand, I made the business successful, which benefits not just me but potentially the family. My mom and granddad support me, which is good, but my dad and sister are against me. It's a tough spot because family relationships are important, and this could cause long-term issues. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have approached him differently, discussed the idea with him, and offered him a partnership from the beginning. That way, he would feel involved and valued, and I wouldn't have to deal with the betrayal aspect. But I also think about the practical side. If I had waited for him to get on board, the business might not have taken off as it did. I'm action-oriented, and he's not. So, maybe I had to make the move quickly to capitalize on the idea before it was too late. Another angle is the legal aspect. I got the IP rights, so legally, I own the idea now. But ethically, is that fair? Did I take something that was his without his consent? Or was it just an idea that he wasn't going to use, so I took the initiative? I also need to consider the emotional impact on my dad. Betrayal is a deep feeling, and it's affecting our relationship. I might have to work on rebuilding trust, even if I think I was right to take the idea. Maybe offering him a bigger share or a more significant role in the business could help, but he's already rejected that. In the end, I think I did what I thought was best for the business and for myself. But I also recognize that my dad's feelings are valid, and I might have handled the situation better by involving him more from the start. It's a tough balance between being proactive and respecting family dynamics.
